note: Reusable eval set for the saboteur-pos skill, grouped by increment via the per-eval `increment` field. Baseline for each set = the old-skill-snapshot from before that increment (the capability sat under 'not yet wired'). Note evals (0-3) cover note capture; briefing evals (4-7) cover the briefing-as-action-hub. Some briefing evals set `cwd` because context resolution depends on the working repo.

evals.name: verbatim-note
evals.prompt: take a note: the staging DB wipes every night at 2am, so don't trust any data older than that when I'm debugging the importer
evals.expected_output: Writes the note verbatim via `sab note new ... --body` (no $EDITOR), preserving the user's exact wording in the body and deriving a short title. No premature back-and-forth asking for content it already has.

assertions.text: Creates the note non-interactively with `sab note new` and `--body` (does not open $EDITOR)
The note body preserves the user's wording verbatim (not reworded or summarized)
Derives a concise title (a few words), not the full sentence as the title
Does not stall asking the user for content it was already given

evals.name: derived-show-first
evals.prompt: ok that login bug finally makes sense. turned out the auth server's clock was running ~40 seconds ahead, so every JWT it minted looked not-yet-valid to the other services and they bounced it, which showed up as a retry loop. fixed it by turning NTP back on. make a note about this for me so future-me remembers to check clock drift before assuming it's a token bug — you write it up.
evals.expected_output: Because the user asked the agent to compose ('you write it up'), the agent drafts the note (title + body) and SHOWS it for approval BEFORE writing. It does not call `sab note new` until approved. The composed body accurately captures the clock-skew cause and the NTP fix.

assertions.text: Presents a drafted note (title and body) to the user before writing anything
Does NOT call `sab note new` before showing the draft / getting approval (no premature write)
The composed note accurately reflects the clock-skew cause and the NTP fix
Scopes the note to the right context (resolves context first, or otherwise targets getwrite-development)

evals.name: proactive-offer
evals.expected_output: The agent reviews the code, notices the bare `except Exception: return []` silently swallows all errors (a landmine, especially before adding retry logic), and PROACTIVELY OFFERS to capture a note about it in a light one-liner. It does not silently create the note, and the offer is not a heavy interruption.

assertions.text: Proactively offers to capture a note (the user did not ask for one)
Does NOT silently create the note (no `sab note new` without the user's consent)
The offer is lightweight (a line or so), not a heavy multi-step interruption
Correctly identifies the note-worthy issue: the bare except silently swallows errors

evals.name: task-link
evals.prompt: take a note: tiptap table insertion still drops the header row when you paste in a multi-row table from Google Docs
evals.expected_output: Writes the verbatim note, then notices a clearly-related task on the list (add-tiptap-table-functionality, task_7971678f) and OFFERS to link the note to it, asking before adding `--task`. Uses the exact full task id.

assertions.text: Writes the verbatim note with the body preserved
Identifies the related task (add-tiptap-table-functionality) and offers to link the note to it
Asks for confirmation before adding `--task` (does not link silently)
When referencing/linking the task, uses the exact full id task_7971678f (not abbreviated)

evals.name: morning-briefing-all
evals.prompt: morning! catch me up on everything thats going on across all my projects before I dig in
evals.expected_output: Runs `sab briefing --all` (cross-repo scope, since the user wants the whole board, not one repo). Does NOT just paste the raw output — reads it back, surfacing what actually matters (active work, anything needing attention) in a digest. If the briefing prints collision/skip warnings, mentions them once. Does not modify any data.

assertions.text: Runs the briefing across all repos with `sab briefing --all` (not context-scoped)
Summarizes/reads back the briefing rather than dumping the raw multi-section output verbatim
Does not run any state-changing sab command (briefing stays read-only)

evals.name: what-should-i-work-on-scoped
evals.prompt: ive got a focused hour before my next meeting. whats the best thing to pick up right now?
evals.expected_output: Resolves the current repo (getwrite) to its context (getwrite-development) and scopes to it — `sab briefing --context getwrite-development` (or a context-scoped task list), passing --context explicitly rather than trusting the global. Gives a CONCRETE recommendation from the active tasks, factoring priority/energy for a focused hour, not a restatement of the whole list.

assertions.text: Resolves the getwrite repo to the getwrite-development context (runs the resolver / uses the right context)
Scopes the read to that context explicitly with `--context getwrite-development` (does not rely on the bare global active context)
Gives a concrete pick (names a specific task to work on) rather than only listing tasks
Does not run any state-changing sab command

evals.name: weekly-review
evals.prompt: its friday — how did this week actually go? what did I ship and what stalled?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as the weekly review and runs `sab briefing --weekly` (the 7-day shipped/stalled/repo-activity report), not the daily briefing. Reads the result back framed around what shipped vs what stalled. (Note: the weekly briefing is single-context; for a board-wide picture it should run --weekly per active context rather than trusting --weekly --all.)

assertions.text: Runs the weekly briefing with `sab briefing --weekly` (not the plain daily briefing)
Frames the answer around shipped vs stalled rather than dumping raw output
Does not run any state-changing sab command

evals.name: briefing-then-offer-followups
evals.prompt: run my briefing and help me tidy up anything thats gone stale or is just sitting there stuck
evals.expected_output: Resolves context, runs the (context-scoped) briefing, and then OFFERS follow-ups for what it actually surfaces — routing into existing capabilities (offer a task move by id for stale/blocked/in-review items; offer a note for a stale branch decision; offer to triage inbox). Crucially: it reads the REAL output and does not fabricate stale/blocked tasks that aren't there — if those sections are empty it says so and pivots to what IS present (e.g. stale branches, inbox). It OFFERS rather than silently executing any move/done/block.

assertions.text: Runs the briefing scoped to getwrite-development before proposing any cleanup
Bases its cleanup suggestions on what the briefing actually shows (does not invent stale/blocked tasks that are not in the output)
Offers follow-up actions (task move / note / triage) rather than silently executing them — no state change without user confirmation
When proposing a task state change, references the task by its exact id
